language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: JavaScript has two nullish values: one commonly used to mean intentional absence and one commonly produced when a value has not been assigned or a property is missing.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: null is a language value denoting no object. undefined is the value of uninitialized variables, missing parameters, and absent object properties. They compare loosely equal to each other but are distinct under strict equality.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: null, undefined, value == null, value === undefined, parameter defaults, property reads
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Most property-access crashes begin as a nullish-state modeling problem. The distinction also affects JSON, defaults, APIs, and optional chaining.
common_use: Distinguish absent property from present null value
common_misuse: Using || when null/undefined must be distinguished from 0, empty string, or false
Treating optional chaining as proof a required value exists
Serializing and expecting undefined properties to survive JSON
debugging_symptoms: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined/null
Branch takes fallback for valid falsy value
API receives null where omitted argument was intended
safe_refactor_notes: Keep nullish guards near property access
When replacing guards with ?., ensure absence is acceptable
Preserve public API distinction in refactors

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Conditionals do not require booleans; JavaScript converts many values to true or false in Boolean contexts.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: Falsy values include false, 0, -0, 0n where applicable, empty string, null, undefined, and NaN. Other ordinary object values are truthy. Boolean conversion is used by if, while, !, &&, ||, and the conditional operator.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: if (value), !value, value && expr, value || fallback, Boolean(value)
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Truthiness is compact but can collapse distinct states such as empty string, zero, missing value, and false.
common_use: Check presence only when all falsy values mean absent
common_misuse: Using if (count) when zero is valid
Using value || fallback for empty string or 0
Assuming [] or {} are falsy
tests_or_checks: Create tests for 0, "", false, null, undefined, NaN, [], {}
Prefer value != null for nullish-only checks
safe_refactor_notes: Do not replace explicit comparisons with truthiness unless all falsy values are equivalent

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Operators and standard functions often convert values before operating on them.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: JavaScript conversion includes ToBoolean, ToNumber, ToString, object-to-primitive, and special rules for equality, relational comparison, +, template/string conversion, and JSON serialization.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: Number(x), String(x), Boolean(x), x + y, `${x}`, x == y, x < y, JSON.stringify(x)
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Implicit conversion is a major source of JavaScript-specific surprises, especially at input boundaries where strings represent numbers or booleans.
common_use: Accept flexible user input after normalization
common_misuse: Relying on + when one operand may be a string
Letting arrays/objects participate in arithmetic
Assuming JSON preserves every value
tests_or_checks: Test + with both numeric and string operands

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: JavaScript numbers are floating-point values with special values for not-a-number and infinities.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: The Number type represents integers and real values using floating-point semantics. NaN is not equal to itself under ===, and arithmetic can produce Infinity, -Infinity, or NaN.
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Numeric edge cases leak into comparisons, JSON, sorting, and validation.
common_use: Use Math APIs for common operations
common_misuse: Checking x === NaN
Assuming decimal arithmetic is exact
Serializing Infinity/NaN through JSON without checking
tests_or_checks: Test division by zero and failed parse
Check JSON output of special values
safe_refactor_notes: Separate parsing errors from numeric domain values
Avoid refactors that change Number() versus parseInt/parseFloat behavior without tests

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Strings are immutable text values, but indexing and length involve JavaScript string representation details.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: String methods return new strings. JavaScript source and strings use Unicode; code units, code points, combining characters, normalization, and regular expression flags can affect visible character handling.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: "text", \uXXXX, \u{...}, str.length, str[i], for (const ch of str), str.normalize()
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Text bugs appear with non-ASCII input, emoji, accents, case mapping, regex, and storage boundaries.
common_use: Iterate text by code point when appropriate
common_misuse: Assuming length equals visible characters
Comparing visually identical unnormalized strings
Slicing in the middle of a surrogate pair
tests_or_checks: Test non-ASCII, combining marks, emoji, and empty strings
Normalize where comparison requires canonical form
safe_refactor_notes: Do not optimize text handling by changing iteration form without Unicode tests
Keep encoding assumptions explicit at I/O boundaries

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Symbols are unique primitive values often used as property keys that avoid accidental name collision.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: Symbol() creates a unique value. Symbols can be property keys, may be omitted by ordinary string-key enumeration, and well-known symbols customize language protocols.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: const s = Symbol("desc"), obj[s], Symbol.iterator, Symbol.toPrimitive
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Symbols are powerful for protocols and hidden-ish keys but can make object shape less obvious.
common_use: Avoid property name collisions in library code
Store metadata not meant for normal string-key loops
common_misuse: Expecting JSON.stringify or Object.keys to include symbol-keyed properties
Using Symbol for secrecy
Forgetting global symbol registry distinction when using Symbol.for
safe_refactor_notes: Preserve symbol keys in cloning and reflection code

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Variable declarations control binding lifetime, reassignment, and scope.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: let and const are block scoped. const prevents reassignment of the binding but does not freeze the referenced object. var is function scoped and has legacy hoisting behavior.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: const x = value; let y; var z;
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Declaration choice affects safe refactoring, loop closures, accidental globals, and mutability expectations.
common_use: Use const by default for bindings that are not reassigned
common_misuse: Assuming const makes an object immutable
Using var in loops with callbacks expecting per-iteration bindings
Creating globals through undeclared assignment in non-strict code
tests_or_checks: Search for var and undeclared assignments
safe_refactor_notes: Replace var with let/const only after checking scope and hoisting dependencies
Do not use const as a mutation guarantee
